independent_reviewer_counterclaim: The strongest objection is that this session did the second-priority work because it had spoiled its claim on the first, and that the sequencing argument I gave for it is self-serving. The brief for PR #103 was the top open item; I read the authoring session's reasoning during orientation, which disqualified me under its own section 0, and then executed two sweeps instead -- one of which (Q1) touches the very tripwire that brief's A2 surface exists to audit. I did leave the tripwire's configuration unchanged and handed F1 forward, but I still swept uses out of its scope before it was audited, which changes what a cold reviewer will find. A reviewer could fairly say the honest move was to stop after orienting, report the contamination, and do nothing that touched PR #103's artifacts at all. A second objection, narrower and possibly right: F1 says the 2026-08-15 boundary probes 'read their result backwards' on Mode-P, but I am inferring intent from a one-line summary in a session record I did not author; the probe may have been scoped to unhyphenated forms deliberately, in which case the finding is a coverage gap and not a misread, and I have stated it more sharply than my evidence supports.
